commits.message:
fix: freemail signature-learning contamination, boilerplate company capture, duplicate requirement clutter

Three real production data-quality bugs, found investigating one
reported draft (a jobs.nvoids.com relay posting):

1. Signature pattern learning (shipped this session) was recording and
   applying corrections keyed only by sender domain, with no distinction
   between a real corporate domain and a shared public mail provider. A
   single correction for one gmail.com sender ("Sekhar U, Sr.IT
   Technical Recruiter, Tekwings LLC") had been silently applied to 741
   unrelated drafts from completely different recruiters who also
   happen to send through gmail.com via the same relay -- fabricating a
   false identity on every one of them. Fixed by excluding a list of
   common freemail domains from both recording and applying learned
   patterns (app/email_parsing/signature_learning.py) -- a sender domain
   only means "one company" for a real corporate domain.

2. The signature parser's company-name detection (COMPANY_SUFFIX_RE)
   matches on words like "technology"/"services"/"solutions" anywhere in
   a short line. A jobs.nvoids.com footer line -- "Keywords: artificial
   intelligence information technology Texas" -- matched on "technology"
   and got captured as the sender's company name. Added a boilerplate-
   line filter (BOILERPLATE_LINE_RE, app/email_parsing/signature.py) for
   the relay's known footer patterns ("Keywords:", "View this job online",
   "Happy recruiting", "Free resume and job search portal", "You received
   this email from") before title/company detection runs on a line.

3. The same relay re-sends the identical requirement under a new
   message id (confirmed: three drafts, byte-identical body, all within
   17 seconds). Exact-content dedupe already detects and links each one
   back to the canonical delivery (metadata.exact_content_duplicate_of)
   -- by design nothing is blocked or deleted, every source message
   still becomes its own draft, for audit. But the review queue was
   still *displaying* every duplicate as if it were a distinct new
   requirement. GET /drafts/summary now excludes exact-content
   duplicates by default (list_draft_summaries, app/drafts/service.py);
   `?include_duplicates=true` still surfaces them, wired to a "Show
   duplicates" checkbox on the drafts list page, with a small "duplicate"
   tag on any row shown that way.

Data cleanup for the 741 already-contaminated drafts and the bad
gmail.com signature_corrections rows is a separate one-time script run
after this deploys, not part of this code change.

New coverage: signature_corrections never gets a row for gmail.com and
apply_learned_signature_patterns is a no-op for it; the exact relay
footer text that caused the company-name bug no longer produces one (or
a fabricated title); GET /drafts/summary hides an exact-content
duplicate by default but still returns it with `is_duplicate: true`
under include_duplicates=true. Full regression suite (18 checks) green
against a fresh schema and rebuilt image; frontend type-checks and
builds clean.
